Subject: Exploring an on-prem path for model serving — initial questionnaire

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team has asked us to validate an on-prem (air-gapped or VPC-isolated) deployment option for high-risk workloads — specifically customer PII processing for loan applications. Before we escalate internally, could you confirm a few high-level things so we can scope a formal RFP: 

- Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations in both VPC and fully on-prem installs?
- Can your runtime be run without any outbound telemetry to Redwood (only customer-controlled endpoints)?
- What audit/logging granularity is available (per-request token-level logs, who-accessed-what, retention windows)?
- Typical packaging for on-prem: container images + orchestration, or OVA/installer?
- Rough resourcing profile: what core team we should expect to work with Redwood for a pilot (SRE, Infra, Security lead) and a notional timeline for a POC?

Attached: GreenBank_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf — filled by their security reviewer; some questions we've not been able to answer. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

Best,
Alex
Alex Barnes
Senior Product Security Manager | GreenBank

Alex — thanks for the clear questions and the questionnaire. Looping in the cross-functional leads to make sure we cover both the product and operational constraints.

Quick summary up front: yes, we can support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and a private-only control plane option for customers who require zero outbound telemetry. There are important caveats and resourcing impacts depending on whether the preference is (A) VPC private deployment with Redwood control plane in customer VPC, (B) fully air-gapped on-prem with customer-managed CI/CD, or (C) a hybrid (dedicated appliances + private control plane).

Notes / asks for internal owners (please reply with estimates and blockers):
- Monica (Product): confirm which Redwood features can be turned off for air-gapped installs (metering, auto-update, model catalog syncing) and what the minimum feature set for GA would look like.
- Markus (Infra): we need a ballpark sizing for a pilot that supports ~50 concurrent inference sessions (peak) for a medium LLM (30B quantized). Include GPU type options and network diagrams for physical isolation.
- Dev (Security/Compliance): need a short checklist for KMS integration patterns we support (AWS CloudHSM, on-prem Thales, KMIP endpoints) and required network ports.
- Lauren (Sales/CS): what's an acceptable pilot success criteria from the commercial side (SLA targets, acceptable go/no-go metrics) and suggested deal path/contractual language for handling data residency and audit access?

Proposed timeline:
- Jan 9–13: internal scoping and draft RFI response (we can use an internal template).
- Jan 16: 60-minute technical deep-dive w/ GreenBank security + infra to walk architecture options.
- Jan 23: POC kickoff if GreenBank approves scope.

I'm attaching a draft RFI response (rfi_response_draft.docx) — please mark edits directly in Drive. Lauren, please add commercial guardrails and a preliminary SOW template.

Karthik
Director, Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: GreenBank on-prem feasibility — initial architecture notes

Karthik / team — quick infra readout based on the ask. High level: doable, but cost and operational complexity vary widely by isolation level. Key points: 

1) Packaging & install model
- Preferred delivery for us: container images + Helm charts for customer-managed K8s (gives repeatability). For fully air-gapped sites we can provide an offline tarball plus an installer script and checksums.

2) KMS/HSM
- We support: AWS CloudHSM (via VPC peering + proxy), KMIP endpoints (Thales), and client-managed HSM appliances behind customer VPN. We will need a short integration sprint (2–3 engineer-weeks) to validate network/proxy configuration for each HSM type.

3) Telemetry & control plane
- Option A (VPC-isolated): control plane components run in the customer VPC. No outbound telemetry to Redwood public endpoints. We still require an admin-level reverse channel for support (optional and can be disabled in contract).
- Option B (Air-gapped): full offline mode — requires dedicated engineering support for updates and patches. Patching cadence becomes manual; expect a 1–2 person ops rotation for customer shadow on deploy.

4) Pilot sizing (provisional)
- For 50 concurrent sessions on a 30B quantized model: recommend 4x A100 80GB nodes (or 6x L4-class for lower perf), 64GB RAM control-plane instances. Network: single-stage NAT inside customer LAN; egress blocked.
- Expected infra engineer time for POC: 3 engineers for 3 weeks (setup, validation, runbook + handoff).

5) Logging & audit
- We can emit locally-stored audit logs with configurable retention. By default includes request-id, model-version, prompt-hash, timestamp, user-id. Token-level logs are supported but should be enabled only under a signed data-retention SLA (legal/privacy implications).

Blockers / open questions:
- SLA: can GreenBank accept that in air-gapped mode we cannot provide realtime hotfixes without shipping artifacts (longer MTTR)?
- Network or procurement constraints for HSM devices — need specifics.
- Legal: any national export controls for the model weights to the customer's country? (Dev/Legal input needed.)

I'll put a short architecture sketch in Drive by EOD.

-Markus
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime | Redwood Inference

Thanks team — this looks reasonable. Commercial notes / next steps from my side: 

- Pilot acceptance criteria: 99th pctl inference latency < 750ms for the defined workload, successful KMS handshake tests, and a dry-run audit demonstrating local log captures.
- Contract template: use Private Deployment SOW v3 with two changes: (1) explicit clause on manual patching cadence for air-gapped installs, (2) liability cap tied to pilot scope. I'll attach redlines to the Drive doc.
- Pricing: recommend a fixed pilot fee (covers 3-weeks infra engineering + one week post-run support) + time-and-materials for ongoing ops after handoff.
- Sales ops ask: please capture expected procurement lead times for HSM hardware (Alex, if you can share vendor/part numbers that will help).

I'll join the Jan 16 technical deep-dive and bring a preliminary SOW and pilot statement of work. Monica — can you produce a minimal feature checklist for air-gapped GA so we can align commercial scope?

Lauren
